name: Send morning briefing to Telegram
description: Sends a daily 08:00 WIB Telegram briefing with Jakarta weather (now + daily forecast) and a quote. Hourly catch-up plus a briefing_log guard covers n8n downtime without duplicate sends.

parameters.notes: One cron rule on purpose: misfire coalescing fires one catch-up per rule, so two rules caused two concurrent runs and a duplicate send.
Why Code: validation + fallback selection + WMO lookup + HTML escaping across two sources is multi-step logic; native Edit Fields would need many brittle expressions.

nodes.name: Check Today's Log
nodes.notes: Idempotency: finds a production send for today's date (WIB).

nodes.name: Already Sent Today?
nodes.notes: Production runs skip if today's briefing was already sent. Manual runs always send.

nodes.name: Log Briefing Sent
nodes.notes: Audit trail + idempotency marker for the catch-up schedule.

nodes.name: Load Settings
nodes.notes: Reads chat ID + API endpoints from the Automation Settings table (replaces $env, which is blocked in nodes).

nodes.name: Ping Healthchecks
nodes.notes: Dead-man's switch: production sends ping the healthchecks.io check; manual runs hit /log so tests don't mark it healthy. URL lives in Automation Settings.

nodeGroups.name: Settings & idempotency guard
nodeGroups.description: Loads chat ID/endpoints from Automation Settings, then stops production runs if today's briefing is already in briefing_log

nodeGroups.name: Compose, deliver & log
nodeGroups.description: Validate + render HTML, send to Telegram, record in briefing_log, then ping healthchecks.io (production only)

versionMetadata.name: Single cron rule (fix duplicate catch-up); healthchecks.io ping
versionMetadata.description: Two schedule rules + misfirePolicy coalesce fired one catch-up per rule after downtime, so two concurrent runs both passed the idempotency check and sent twice (exec 96/97, 2026-11-17). Merged into one cron rule 0 8-20 * * *. Added Ping Healthchecks after a logged send: production pings the check, manual runs hit /log (event only, no status change).
